chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Ibn Miskān, from ʿAnbasah ibn Muṣʿab, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man had a wet dream, then when morning came he looked at his garment and did not see anything on it. He said: He may perform salat (prayer) in it. I said: Then what about a man who saw in a dream that he had a wet dream, then when he rose he found a small amount of moisture on the tip of his private part? He said: Ghusl is not obligatory upon him. Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: Ghusl is only from the greater fluid. And it indicates also that the ruling of the sick person differs from the ruling of the healthy person.

key_terms.الْعَلِيلِ: the sick or medically impaired person
key_terms.الْمَاءِ الْأَكْبَرِ: the major fluid, meaning semen in this context
key_terms.بَلَلًا: a trace of moisture or dampness
key_terms.غُسْلٌ: ritual bath required for major ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: When is ghusl required after seeing a wet dream in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses rulings related to suspected seminal discharge after sleep and whether ghusl is obligatory. It indicates that merely seeing a dream or finding slight moisture does not necessitate ghusl unless the greater fluid is present, and it also notes a distinction between the ruling of the sick and the healthy.
